nodes.label: Real vs Simulated Boundary
nodes.rationale: Mayall does not fork mainnet and does not claim to. The chain state and funds are a local simulation; that distinction is the product, not a footnote.

nodes.label: House Rules for App Screens
nodes.rationale: The page house rules were written for pages read once, and part of what they ban is the structure of a working screen, so 1px borders, row rules, small labels and repeated panels relax here — with limits, while gradients, glows, glass and rainbow charts stay banned.

nodes.label: Banned Palette Families (cream/terracotta, violet/indigo)
nodes.rationale: One studied site in 246 has a terracotta primary button and none has a violet one; those are colours of generated pages, not of the gallery. Warmth is not beige.

nodes.label: Colour Proportion Rule
nodes.rationale: Ground 70–90%, accent under 5% of any screen: the moment the accent appears in five places it stops meaning 'here'.

nodes.label: Slide 8 - What We Would Build Next
nodes.norm_label: slide 8 - what we would build next

nodes.label: Evidence Rendered Verbatim
nodes.rationale: A finding is only as strong as the evidence it lists; the report renders that evidence verbatim.

nodes.label: Argument-First Copy Deck
nodes.rationale: A section with no claim is filler; delete it. The order of the argument is the order of the page, which is how the stock hero/logos/features/pricing sequence is avoided.

nodes.label: Two-Line Headline Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: The constraint is arithmetic, so do it before falling in love with a sentence: about 32 characters survives every viewport at a confident size.

nodes.label: Two-Line Headline Rule
nodes.rationale: In blind tests a sentence set big over three or more lines was read as a long headline every time, whatever its markup — so the rule is two lines or fewer at every width.

nodes.label: Detector Confidence Cap Policy
nodes.rationale: Confidence is the maximum of the evidence floors a rule triggered - never a sum - and every rule is capped below 1.0.

nodes.label: Drawing the Subject
nodes.rationale: In testing, pages that drew their subject with care beat pages that borrowed unrelated photographs every time, and beat pages that showed nothing.

nodes.label: Imagery Preference Ladder
nodes.rationale: Order of preference: the project's own images, generated images, real pictures of the subject's world from open collections, drawings from the subject, dealt photographs, then type and colour alone — each step chosen because the honest picture beats the borrowed one.

nodes.label: Footage Selection
nodes.rationale: Only 31% of studied clips had a poster and the panel recorded the blank grey boxes before they played as faults, so a poster is required here.

nodes.label: Evidence-Weighted Confidence Model
nodes.rationale: Each rule accumulates independent signals and the score is the maximum of the floors it triggered; signals are never summed, and per-detector caps sit between 0.93 and 0.98.

nodes.label: Narrative Keyword Limitation
nodes.rationale: Detectors fire partly on how the incident is described, not only on what the EVM executed; a misleading rootCause string can raise confidence, so treat confidence as a triage signal.

nodes.label: Contingency: Written Case Instead of Live Run
nodes.norm_label: contingency: written case instead of live run
nodes.rationale: If the live run fails on stage, do not debug; fall back to the curve-v2-reentrancy case page, which carries the same reentrancy scenario.

nodes.label: Honesty Slide: What Is Real vs Simulated
nodes.norm_label: honesty slide: what is real vs simulated
nodes.rationale: The contracts are real Solidity and the execution is a real EVM via Foundry, but the chain state is local; Mayall does not fork mainnet and does not claim to.

nodes.label: Accordion / Collapse Recipe
nodes.rationale: Height is the tolerated layout animation because an accordion has no transform equivalent; the duration stays short since it costs layout on every frame.

nodes.label: Scroll Reveal Recipe
nodes.rationale: Marketing surfaces only, fired once: re-animating on every scroll-by is an interface fighting its reader.

nodes.label: Drag to Dismiss Recipe
nodes.rationale: Springs rather than durations, because the user can reverse mid-motion and an interrupted drag must keep its velocity.

nodes.label: Hold to Confirm Recipe
nodes.rationale: Asymmetric timing on purpose: 2s linear on the deliberate press (the fill is progress, so it must not ease), 200ms ease-out on release.

nodes.label: Modal Recipe
nodes.rationale: The one popover that stays centred: a modal is exempt from trigger-anchored transform-origin because it is not anchored to a trigger.

nodes.label: Dropdown / Popover / Menu Recipe
nodes.rationale: The panel must scale out of its trigger (transform-origin: var(--transform-origin)), because looking like it came out of the thing you clicked is the whole point of the animation.

nodes.label: Toast Recipe
nodes.rationale: Uses plain ease rather than ease-out and runs slightly slower than typical UI, because Sonner reads as elegant when its motion is tuned to the component's personality rather than to the generic UI budget.

nodes.label: Animation Build Sequence
nodes.rationale: Steps 1 and 2 gate everything: whether it should animate at all, then what purpose it serves. Reaching for a curve before those are answered is the failure mode the sequence exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Easing Tokens (--ease-out, --ease-in-out, --ease-drawer)
nodes.rationale: Built-in CSS easings are too weak; named bezier tokens keep every curve decided rather than invented per component.

nodes.label: Frequency Gate
nodes.rationale: Animation justified by frequency of exposure: nothing at 100+ times a day, near-imperceptible at tens a day, standard at occasional, delight only at rare. It exists to produce zero lines of code sometimes, and that is a success.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion and Pointer Gating
nodes.rationale: Ships with the animation, never as a follow-up: reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not zero, and hover styling is gated on (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) because touch fires false hovers.

nodes.label: Cheapest-Tool Selection
nodes.rationale: Walk down CSS transition, @starting-style, CSS animation, WAAPI, Motion and stop at the first that fits: don't install a motion library for a fade. CSS wins for predetermined motion because it runs off the main thread.

nodes.label: Forensic View (trace, storage diff, gas flame)
nodes.norm_label: forensic view (trace, storage diff, gas flame)

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Static Deployment
nodes.rationale: Pages is static hosting, so the deployed site is a reading surface for evidence produced locally; the live Foundry simulation stays local-only by design and degrades to a run-this-locally state.

nodes.label: Collateral Price Manipulation
nodes.rationale: The protocol trusted a number it did not control — the price of the collateral being liquidated — and the attacker controlled it for the length of a single transaction.

nodes.label: Trace Asymmetry (explorer view vs call tree)
nodes.norm_label: trace asymmetry (explorer view vs call tree)
nodes.rationale: An explorer shows two ordinary transactions and a large transfer; the trace shows one transaction in which a function is called seven times and the price is wrong on the last six. That difference, not the loss figure, is what turns an event into a case.

nodes.label: Checks-Effects-Interactions Ordering
nodes.rationale: Zero balances[msg.sender] before the transfer: because the balance is only cleared after the external call returns, each nested call passes the same check and is paid again.

nodes.label: Insolvency by Accounting
nodes.rationale: totalWithdrawn moves 0 to 6 ETH while totalDeposited sits at 11 ETH, so the books claim 11 ETH against a physical balance of 4 ETH — the contract is insolvent by 7 ETH and the depositor cannot be made whole.

nodes.label: Nesting Signature of the Exploit
nodes.rationale: ReentrancyVault::withdraw() invoked seven times — the initial call plus six re-entries — each nesting deeper, with ReentrancyAttacker::receive() between every pair. That nesting pattern is the signature the detector raises at 97% confidence.

nodes.label: SHA-256 Chain-of-Custody Manifest
nodes.rationale: The bundle ships a SHA-256 manifest so the exported evidence can be shown to be the bytes that were produced, which is what makes the export court-ready rather than merely convenient.

nodes.label: Forensic Simulation Engine
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Foundry CLI so an exploit proof-of-concept runs against deliberately vulnerable contracts in a real EVM, capturing the full call tree, gas profile and storage mutations instead of inferring them from a block explorer.

nodes.label: Deterministic Narrative Fallback
nodes.rationale: Without MINIMAX_API_KEY the summary falls back to a deterministic generator and is never presented as an AI-authored report — honesty about provenance.

nodes.label: Pattern Detectors (ten detectors)
nodes.rationale: Ten detectors run over every simulation and each emits a confidence score, severity, human-readable evidence pointers and a Mermaid attack flow, so a classification is defensible rather than asserted.

nodes.label: Avoidance Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: A page with every tell removed and nothing put in their place is an empty page with good manners, and that is a tell too.

nodes.label: Order of Work: Idea Before Checks
nodes.norm_label: order of work: idea before checks
nodes.rationale: The order of work in SKILL.md fills the gap the tells were covering: idea from the subject, dealt composition, real pictures or committed type, then the checks.

nodes.label: Tells Registry (Dated Design Ant-patterns)
nodes.rationale: The registry is deliberately dated because every published 'use this instead' list becomes the next wave of tells; replacements here are procedures, not products.

nodes.label: Size Contrast Is the Lever, Weight Is Not
nodes.norm_label: size contrast is the lever, weight is not
nodes.rationale: Half of the studied heroes are set in a regular weight; scale and spacing make type confident, bold is one option among several.

nodes.label: Type Scale: Few Sizes, Far Apart
nodes.norm_label: type scale: few sizes, far apart
nodes.rationale: About 30 of the 114 strongest sites used two or three sizes with nothing in between and none used a graded five- or six-step scale; nine near-equal sizes read as mush.

nodes.label: Attack Replay Motion Piece
nodes.rationale: Every frame is a pure function of time with an authored storyboard, not a pile of effects; the console has one authored motion piece and it is the point of the product.

nodes.label: Forensic Instrument in a Dark Lab
nodes.norm_label: forensic instrument in a dark lab
nodes.rationale: The reference is an autopsy room and an oscilloscope, not a fintech app: cold darkness, one hot signal colour, bone-white chrome, every number treated as a measurement.

nodes.label: det-front-running (Ordering / Front Running)
nodes.rationale: A single-transaction local simulation cannot observe mempool ordering; the detector infers it, it does not detect it.

nodes.label: det-logic (Invariant / Logic Error)
nodes.rationale: Effectively totally narrative-dependent: without a keyword hit confidence stays at 0.50 and the detector returns nothing.

nodes.label: Detectors Are Heuristics, Not Proofs
nodes.rationale: They are heuristics over a single transaction: no bytecode reading, no symbolic execution, no mempool observation. A finding is a triage hypothesis with attached evidence.

nodes.label: Evidence Floors Model
nodes.rationale: Confidence is the maximum of the evidence floors a rule triggered, never a sum, and every rule has a cap below 1.0.

nodes.label: Shared Narrative Corpus Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Every detector reads traceText plus the artifact narrative because the artifact names the mechanism; the cost is that a misleading narrative can raise a score.

nodes.label: Arterial Wipe Transition
nodes.rationale: The one authored moment: a subtle arterial wipe on every slide transition.

nodes.label: Evidence Grid Background
nodes.rationale: The evidence grid is a measuring surface, never a decoration.

nodes.label: Print Mode
nodes.rationale: One slide per 1280 x 720 page, in colour, with print-color-adjust exact.

nodes.label: Red Room Design Language
nodes.rationale: Red Room design language on a 1280 x 720 stage scaled to fit; self-contained with no CDN, no webfonts, no network.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion Support
nodes.rationale: prefers-reduced-motion kills the wipe and every transition.

nodes.label: Still Mode
nodes.rationale: Still mode exists for slide-by-slide screenshots; hides HUD, rail and click zones.

nodes.label: Blind Test Rounds
nodes.rationale: Five rounds of blind tests against a no-skill baseline and another design skill were recorded so the rules come from measured outcomes rather than taste alone.

nodes.label: Empty Space Rule (rest vs hole)
nodes.rationale: A void is placed when something closes it (the picture, the type, a tone step, a flat field); about one closer in five in the study is a hairline, and that device is banned here, so the closing has to be done with space and material.

nodes.label: Frame Rules (margins, balance, titles)
nodes.rationale: The frame is what readers judge before any detail ('no good margin', 'everything is shifted to one side', 'no clear title'), and no strong page in the study was pushed to one side.

nodes.label: Main Study: 247 Gallery Sites
nodes.rationale: 248 sites captured 5 October 2026 from One Page Love and Awwwards, scored by 21 model reviewers the Awwwards way; the numbers throughout the skill are these measurements and nothing is rounded up.

nodes.label: October 2026 Study: 100 Sites of the Day
nodes.norm_label: october 2026 study: 100 sites of the day

nodes.label: Type Scale
nodes.rationale: About 30 of the 114 strongest sites use two or three sizes with nothing in between and none uses a graded five-step scale; nine sizes that are all near each other read as mush.

nodes.label: console.log / console2.log
nodes.rationale: console2.sol is recommended over console.sol because a bug in console.sol leaves uint256 and int256 logs undecoded in Forge traces.

nodes.label: stdStorage
nodes.rationale: It finds and writes the storage slot for a variable without knowing the storage layout, by recording every SLOAD and SSTORE during a call; packed slots can be found but not safely written, which is the documented caveat.

nodes.label: Bug Report Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Version, platform, code snippet and concrete reproduction steps, with the snippet as minimal as possible, so the bug can be ruled in or out of the reporter's own project.

nodes.label: Rust Code of Conduct
nodes.rationale: Adopted wholesale so the code of conduct describes the minimum behaviour expected from all contributors rather than being written bespoke.

nodes.label: Pull Request Review Etiquette
nodes.rationale: Only incremental improvement is needed to land a PR; request changes rather than demand them, and do not assume the submitter already knows how to add a test or run a benchmark.

nodes.label: State Update After Transfer Flaw
nodes.rationale: Root cause: withdraw() transfers ETH before zeroing balances[msg.sender], so a malicious receiver re-enters and the vault pays the same balance repeatedly.

nodes.label: App Screen Run
nodes.rationale: An app screen is worked in rather than read, so it gets its own run: inventory the data and jobs, name the screen's one question, choose a style, build the shell, render the data, build the states, then check.

nodes.label: Chart Rules
nodes.rationale: One question, one series; 3–5 faint gridlines; no y-axis line; no legend for a single series; the one hue goes on the screen's main data element because an all-ink screen reads as a kit.

nodes.label: KPI Rules
nodes.rationale: 0 of 23 screens puts an icon in a coloured circle or a sparkline on a KPI; the default is one container split by 1px dividers, value 16–40px, label above.

nodes.label: Shell Archetypes (five)
nodes.rationale: Open plane, tinted frame with a white sheet, ruled T-frame, icon rail and no sidebar; no screen in the study puts a dark or saturated sidebar against a light canvas (0 of 17).

nodes.label: Table and List Rules
nodes.rationale: No zebra striping (0 of 23), 12px sentence-case grey headers with no fill band, numbers right-aligned in tabular figures with fixed decimals per metric.

nodes.label: Idea from the Subject
nodes.rationale: In the study a concept taken from the thing itself, not the styling, separated the best sites from the forgettable ones; pages that lost had a good composition with a category idea.

nodes.label: Look-and-Fix Loop
nodes.rationale: Passing the inspector means nothing banned was measured, not that the page is good; the screenshots are judged on the pictures only, because if a problem is visible in a screenshot it is real whatever the code says.

nodes.label: One Live Thing
nodes.rationale: Every winning page in blind tests had one thing the visitor can do or that differs each visit, and jurors named it first.

nodes.label: The Run (ten-step build)
nodes.rationale: Steps 1–5 decide whether the page is any good; the rest execute. The order exists so the idea is filled in before any markup.

nodes.label: Block Explorer Gap
nodes.rationale: Explorers show that something happened; incident responders need how. A block explorer gives the transaction, the value moved and the addresses, but not the call that re-entered, the slot that was rewritten, or the invariant that stopped holding.

nodes.label: Honest limitation: local EVM, no mainnet fork
nodes.norm_label: honest limitation: local evm, no mainnet fork

nodes.label: Fourteen Critique Passes
nodes.rationale: Judge the screenshots, never the code: you wrote the code, so you will read your intentions into it; the pictures only show what is there.

nodes.label: Avoidance Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: A page with every tell removed and nothing put in their place is an empty page with good manners, and that is a tell too; the tells were filling a gap where an idea should have been.

nodes.label: Dated Tells Registry
nodes.rationale: The registry is dated and never names a replacement font, colour or component: every published 'use this instead' list has become the next wave of tells within months, so replacements are procedures, not products.

nodes.label: House Rules (no-ornament style)
nodes.rationale: Some rules are what the study measured (icon cards 1% vs 28% on weak sites, gradients 22% vs 52%); monospace labels, index numbers and hairlines are banned against the data, by the owner's decision, precisely because generators copy them first and they now read as costume.

nodes.label: Storage Diff Capture Strategy
nodes.rationale: Storage mutation capture is cheatcode-based inside the proof-of-concept test rather than reconstructed from RPC, because the chain state is local and controlled.

nodes.label: Motion Budget
nodes.rationale: A page that does not move reads as a mock-up (the inspector fails under eight moving elements), but the same fade-and-slide on every block is the most cited motion tell of generated pages.

nodes.label: Motion Recipes
nodes.rationale: Every recipe keeps content visible when JavaScript is off and puts the hidden state inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so the reduced page is the finished page.

nodes.label: Motion Tokens (--ease-out, --ease-expo, --t-reveal)
nodes.rationale: Curves chosen from what actually ran on 99 studied sites: expo out leads the long reveals, quint out the UI, quart in-out the wipes; the framework default and overshoot curves are deliberately not adopted.

nodes.label: Scroll Scene
nodes.rationale: A tall section whose sticky stage holds still while the page scrolls past, scrubbed 0–1 by that scroll. Nothing captures the wheel: the scrollbar always tells the truth and the scene ends.

nodes.label: App Screen Phone Rules
nodes.rationale: House rule built from the skill's phone rules because the study has no phone screens: navigation folds, KPIs become a 2-column grid or a divided list, tables become two-line rows below about 640px.

nodes.label: Empty, Zero, Loading and Error States
nodes.norm_label: empty, zero, loading and error states
nodes.rationale: Zeros print as zeros, missing values as a grey dash, and an empty section keeps its frame and header; a page that only works with full data is half built.
